text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Adopt the forked and audited **Claude Self-Improvement Skill Pack** as the default for all self-improvement tasks. It’s already been vetted for safety and efficiency, cutting the original’s verbosity by 5% without losing clarity—directly improving task throughput. The trade-off is accepting a 5% verbosity reduction in a pilot run, which risks minor misinterpretation if edge cases appear. This is the fastest path to reliable, audited improvements.

name: Gauge
text: The forked Skill Pack’s 5% efficiency gain is unproven in production—community audits don’t replace real-world stress tests. A safer alternative: run a controlled A/B test on a non-critical self-improvement task, measuring both output quality and speed before committing. Settle it with data: if the fork outperforms the original by 5%+ in a live task, adopt it; otherwise, drop the idea.
